records.source: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֛ק שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בֶן־דָּוִ֖יד עַל־מַלְכוּת֑וֹ וַיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַֽיְגַדְּלֵ֖הוּ לְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And strengthened himself Solomon son of David over his kingdom, and Yahweh his God [was] with him and made him great upward.
pieces: Solomon son of David established himself firmly over his kingdom. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} his God was with him and made him very great.

L.1: And Solomon son of David strengthened himself over his kingdom, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God [was] with him and made him exceedingly great.

R.1: Solomon, David's son, took firm control of his kingdom. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} his God was with him and made him a very great king.

decisions.choice: strengthened himself over his kingdom: made his rule secure
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow strong or to take a firm hold. Said of a new king, it means that he made his hold on the kingdom secure (compare 12:13; 13:21). Kings says the same in other words: "the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon" (1 Kings 2:12, 46).

decisions.choice: the story goes on from 1 Chronicles 29
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles ends with Solomon made king a second time, sitting on Yahweh's throne, and Yahweh making him exceedingly great (1 Chronicles 29:22-25). 2 Chronicles begins where that leaves off. It does not tell the struggle for the throne and the deaths that secured it, which Kings tells (1 Kings 1-2).

decisions.choice: Yahweh his God was with him and made him great: Solomon's greatness is God's gift
decisions.reason: The verse gives the credit for Solomon's rise to Yahweh. "Yahweh was with him" was said of David too (1 Chronicles 11:9; 17:2, 8), and "made him great upward" means "made him exceedingly great", as in 1 Chronicles 29:25.

decisions.choice: made him a very great king
decisions.reason: Readable adds "king" so that it is clear that Solomon's greatness as a ruler is meant.

records.heading: Solomon asks for wisdom

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל לְשָׂרֵי֩ הָאֲלָפִ֨ים וְהַמֵּא֜וֹת וְלַשֹּֽׁפְטִ֗ים וּלְכֹ֛ל נָשִׂ֥יא לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל רָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָבֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And spoke Solomon to all Israel, to [the] commanders of the thousands and the hundreds, and to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, [the] heads of the fathers.
pieces: Solomon addressed all Israel: the commanders over thousands and over hundreds, the judges, and every leader in all Israel, the heads of families.

L.2: And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of the thousands and of the hundreds, and to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the fathers.

R.2: Solomon called on all the people of Israel to come with him. He spoke to the commanders over thousands and over hundreds of soldiers, to the judges, and to all the leaders in Israel, the heads of the families.

decisions.choice: spoke to all Israel: called them together
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word for "say" or "speak". Here no words are quoted: what follows (verse 3) shows that Solomon called the people's leaders to go with him to Gibeon. David had gathered the leaders in the same way to bring up the ark (1 Chronicles 13:1-5).

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and of hundreds: the army's officers
decisions.reason: Israel's fighting men were organized in units of a thousand and of a hundred, each under its commander (1 Chronicles 13:1; 27:1). The list names the army's officers, the judges and the heads of the families: the people's whole leadership stands for "all Israel".

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: the heads of the families
decisions.reason: "House of the fathers" is the family line; its "heads" are the senior men of each family, who spoke for it. The phrase sums up the leaders just named.

decisions.choice: commanders (all levels); leader; heads of the fathers (Literal), heads of families (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books. Readable adds "of soldiers" so that the units are clear.

decisions.choice: called on all the people of Israel to come with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what Solomon's speaking was for (m1), which verse 3 shows.

records.source: וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ וְכָל־הַקָּהָ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ לַבָּמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּגִבְע֑וֹן כִּי־שָׁ֣ם הָיָ֗ה אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה מֹשֶׁ֥ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֖ה בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And went Solomon and all the assembly with him to the high place that [was] at Gibeon, for there was [the] tent of meeting of God which made Moses [the] servant of Yahweh in the wilderness.
pieces: Then Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, because God's tent of meeting was there, the one that Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made in the wilderness.

L.3: And Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place that [was] at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made in the wilderness.

R.3: Then Solomon and all the people gathered with him went to the hilltop shrine at the town of Gibeon. God's meeting tent was there, the one that Moses, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s servant, had made in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: the visit to Gibeon told in 1 Kings 3:4
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 3:4 says that the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice, "because it was the great high place". Chronicles tells the same visit with differences: the whole assembly goes with Solomon, and the reason given is that the tent of meeting Moses made was at Gibeon. It leaves out the remark that the people and Solomon were still sacrificing at the high places (1 Kings 3:2-3).

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting at Gibeon: the tabernacle of the wilderness
decisions.reason: The tent of meeting is the tabernacle Moses made at Sinai (Exodus 33:7; 40:2). By David's time it stood at the high place at Gibeon, a few miles northwest of Jerusalem, and the priests served at its altar there (1 Chronicles 16:39-40; 21:29). That is why Gibeon was the chief place of worship.

decisions.choice: Moses the servant of Yahweh: a title of honor
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a slave, a person who belongs to a master. As a title for Moses it is an honor: he belonged to Yahweh and served him (Deuteronomy 34:5; 1 Chronicles 6:34).

decisions.choice: high place (Literal, Balanced), hilltop shrine (Readable); tent of meeting (Literal, Balanced), meeting tent (Readable); slave (Literal), servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books, as in 1 Kings 3:4.

records.source: אֲבָ֗ל אֲר֤וֹן הָאֱלֹהִים֙ הֶעֱלָ֤ה דָוִיד֙ מִקִּרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֔ים בַּֽהֵכִ֥ין ל֖וֹ דָּוִ֑יד כִּ֧י נָֽטָה־ל֛וֹ אֹ֖הֶל בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: But [the] ark of God had brought up David from Kiriath-jearim to [the place] prepared for it David, for he had pitched for it a tent in Jerusalem.
pieces: But David had brought the ark of God up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

L.4: But the ark of God David had brought up from Kiriath-jearim to [the place] David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

R.4: But David had already brought the ark of God, the sacred chest, up from the town of Kiriath-jearim. He had set up a tent for it in Jerusalem, in a place he had prepared for it.

decisions.choice: the ark brought to Jerusalem: 1 Chronicles 13-16
decisions.reason: David first tried to bring the ark from Kiriath-jearim (1 Chronicles 13:5-6), and then brought it to Jerusalem and put it in the tent he had pitched for it (1 Chronicles 15:1; 16:1; 2 Samuel 6:17).

decisions.choice: but the ark: two places of worship
decisions.reason: In Solomon's day the ark and the tent of meeting were in different places: the ark in a tent in Jerusalem, the old tent and its bronze altar at Gibeon. The verse explains why Solomon sacrificed at Gibeon, where the altar was, though the ark was in Jerusalem. The temple would bring them together (5:2-5).

decisions.choice: to [the place] David had prepared: a short relative clause
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the preposition straight to the verb, "to he-prepared-for-it". It means "to the place David had prepared for it", as 1 Chronicles 15:1, 3 say.

decisions.choice: the ark of God, the sacred chest
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ark once: it was the sacred chest of the covenant.

records.source: וּמִזְבַּ֣ח הַנְּחֹ֗שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ בְּצַלְאֵל֙ בֶּן־אוּרִ֣י בֶן־ח֔וּר שָׂ֕ם לִפְנֵ֖י מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּדְרְשֵׁ֥הוּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וְהַקָּהָֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] altar of the bronze which had made Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur he had put before [the] tabernacle of Yahweh; and sought him Solomon and the assembly.
pieces: Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made the bronze altar and set it in front of the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and there Solomon and the assembly sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.5: And the altar of bronze that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made, he had put before the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and Solomon and the assembly sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.5: Bezalel, the son of Uri and grandson of Hur, had made the bronze altar and set it in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s tabernacle. There Solomon and the people came to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he had put
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text reads a word meaning "he had put": Bezalel set the altar before the tabernacle. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek and Latin translations read a word that differs by one dot and means "there": "the bronze altar ... was there before the tabernacle". Either way the altar stood at Gibeon.

decisions.choice: the bronze altar of Bezalel: the altar of the wilderness
decisions.reason: Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, was the craftsman Yahweh chose to make the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 31:2-5), and he made the bronze altar for burnt offerings (Exodus 38:1-2). 1 Kings 3:4 says only "that altar"; Chronicles names it, to show that Solomon worshiped at the altar Yahweh had commanded.

decisions.choice: sought him: sought Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word "him" can point back to Yahweh, named just before, or to the altar: "sought it out", that is, went to it. Seeking Yahweh, turning to him in worship and asking his help, is a favorite theme of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 16:11; 22:19; 2 Chronicles 7:14), and verses 6-7 show Solomon worshiping and God answering. Those who read "it" take the clause as Solomon and the assembly going to the altar.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of Yahweh: the tent of meeting
decisions.reason: The tabernacle and the tent of meeting (verse 3) are the same tent (Exodus 40:2). The bronze altar stood in its courtyard, before its entrance (Exodus 40:6).

decisions.choice: Bezalel ... had made the bronze altar and set it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the altar first for emphasis. Balanced and Readable make Bezalel the subject so that "he had put" reads naturally.

decisions.choice: there ... sought him (Balanced); came to seek the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "there", which the context implies. Readable names the LORD for "him" so that it is not read as Bezalel (m3).

records.source: וַיַּעַל֩ שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה שָׁ֜ם עַל־מִזְבַּ֤ח הַנְּחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיַּ֧עַל עָלָ֛יו עֹל֖וֹת אָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: And went up Solomon there to [the] altar of the bronze before Yahweh, which [was] at [the] tent of meeting, and offered up on it burnt offerings a thousand.
pieces: There Solomon went up to the bronze altar before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the tent of meeting, and he offered up a thousand burnt offerings on it.

L.6: And Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which [was] at the tent of meeting, and he offered up on it a thousand burnt offerings.

R.6: Solomon went up to the bronze altar at the meeting tent, where he stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar there.

decisions.choice: a thousand burnt offerings, as in 1 Kings 3:4
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 3:4 says that Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings "on that altar". Chronicles says which altar it was: the bronze altar at the tent of meeting (verse 5).

decisions.choice: which was at the tent of meeting: the altar belonged to the tent
decisions.reason: The words "which [was] at the tent of meeting" describe the altar: it was the altar of the tent, standing before it. "Before Yahweh" says that worship there was done in his presence.

decisions.choice: went up; a thousand burnt offerings
decisions.reason: One went up to an altar, which stood raised above the ground. A burnt offering was burned whole; a thousand of them show a king's generous devotion, and would have been burned over several days (compare 1 Kings 3:4).

decisions.choice: where he stood before the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "before the LORD" means here: Solomon worshiped in his presence.

records.source: בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ שְׁאַ֖ל מָ֥ה אֶתֶּן־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: In the night, that [one], appeared God to Solomon and said to him, Ask what I shall give to you.
pieces: That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask for whatever you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to give you."

L.7: In that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."

R.7: That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for anything you want, and I will give it to you."

decisions.choice: God appeared that night: 1 Kings 3:5 without the dream
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 3:5 says that Yahweh appeared to Solomon at Gibeon "in a dream of the night", and 3:15 says that he woke and knew it had been a dream. Chronicles says "God" appeared "in that night" and does not mention a dream. God's words are the same in both.

decisions.choice: Ask what I shall give you: an open offer
decisions.reason: God does not limit what Solomon may ask. The offer shows what Solomon most wants, and his answer pleases God (verse 11; 1 Kings 3:10).

decisions.choice: Ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for anything you want, and I will give it to you.
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 3:5: Readable spells out the offer as a promise, which is what the question means here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים אַתָּ֗ה עָשִׂ֛יתָ עִם־דָּוִ֥יד אָבִ֖י חֶ֣סֶד גָּד֑וֹל וְהִמְלַכְתַּ֖נִי תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Solomon to God, You have done with David my father steadfast love great, and made me king in his place.
pieces: Solomon said to God, "You showed great faithful love to my father David, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have put me on the throne in his place.

L.8: And Solomon said to God, "You have shown great steadfast love to David my father, and have made me king in his place.

R.8: Solomon answered God, "You showed great faithful love to my father David. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me the king who takes his place.

decisions.choice: great steadfast love: loyal kindness that keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word names love that is loyal to a bond and keeps its promises. Yahweh had promised David a son on his throne and a love that would not be taken away from him (1 Chronicles 17:11-13). Solomon sees that promise kept in himself.

decisions.choice: Solomon's prayer, shorter than in 1 Kings 3:6-7
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 3:6 has the same opening words, but there Solomon also calls David Yahweh's servant and speaks of how David walked before him in faithfulness and righteousness. Chronicles gives only the love shown to David and joins to it "you have made me king in his place" (compare 1 Kings 3:7). It also leaves out Solomon's words about being a little boy.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books, as in 1 Kings 3:6.

records.source: עַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים יֵֽאָמֵן֙ דְּבָ֣רְךָ֔ עִ֖ם דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑י כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ הִמְלַכְתַּ֔נִי עַל־עַ֕ם רַ֖ב כַּעֲפַ֥ר הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Now, Yahweh God, let be confirmed your word with David my father, for you have made me king over a people numerous like the dust of the earth.
pieces: Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise to my father David prove true, since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me king over a people as many as the dust of the earth.

L.9: Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word to David my father be confirmed, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me king over a people as many as the dust of the earth.

R.9: Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, please keep the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made to my father David. You have made me king over a people as countless as the dust of the earth.

decisions.choice: let your word be confirmed: let your promise prove true
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made firm, shown to be true. "Your word" is Yahweh's promise to David that his son would reign and build the house (1 Chronicles 17:11-14). David prayed in the same words that the promise be confirmed (1 Chronicles 17:23-24); Solomon asks that it go on coming true in him.

decisions.choice: a people as many as the dust of the earth: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised Abraham and Jacob descendants as many as the dust of the earth (Genesis 13:16; 28:14). 1 Kings 3:8 says instead "a great people, who cannot be numbered"; Chronicles uses the words of the promise itself.

decisions.choice: promise (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "word"; Balanced and Readable say "promise", which is what the word was (m1).

decisions.choice: please keep the promise
decisions.reason: Readable turns the wish "let it be confirmed" into a request to God, which is what it is.

records.source: עַתָּ֗ה חָכְמָ֤ה וּמַדָּע֙ תֶּן־לִ֔י וְאֵֽצְאָ֛ה לִפְנֵ֥י הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה וְאָב֑וֹאָה כִּֽי־מִ֣י יִשְׁפֹּ֔ט אֶת־עַמְּךָ֥ הַזֶּ֖ה הַגָּדֽוֹל׃ס
records.gloss: Now wisdom and knowledge give to me, and I will go out before this people and I will come in; for who will judge your people, this great [one]?
pieces: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out and come in before this people as their leader. For who can judge this great people of {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}?"

L.10: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out before this people and come in; for who can judge this great people of {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}?"

R.10: Give me wisdom and knowledge so that I can lead this people. Who could ever judge this great people of {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}?"

decisions.choice: wisdom and knowledge: Solomon's request in other words than 1 Kings 3:9
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 3:9 Solomon asks for "a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil". Here he asks for "wisdom and knowledge", and the phrase "to go out and come in", which in Kings belongs to his confession that he does not know how (1 Kings 3:7), becomes the purpose of his request. The closing question is much the same, but Kings calls the people "heavy" and Chronicles "great".

decisions.choice: knowledge: understanding, insight
decisions.reason: The word is a rare one, found also in Daniel 1:4, 17 and Ecclesiastes 10:20. It means knowledge or understanding, the ability to grasp what is going on and see what should be done. With "wisdom" it names the skill a ruler needs.

decisions.choice: go out and come in before this people: lead them
decisions.reason: To go out and come in before a people is to lead them in war and in peace, in all their affairs (Numbers 27:17; 1 Samuel 18:16; 1 Chronicles 11:2).

decisions.choice: judge: govern and settle disputes
decisions.reason: The king's judging includes ruling the people and deciding their cases with justice (1 Kings 3:9, 28).

decisions.choice: go out and come in ... as their leader (Balanced); lead (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 3:7: Balanced keeps the picture and adds what it means; Readable says only what it means (m3).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר־אֱלֹהִ֣ים׀לִשְׁלֹמֹ֡ה יַ֣עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיְתָ֨ה זֹ֜את עִם־לְבָבֶ֗ךָ וְלֹֽא־שָׁ֠אַלְתָּ עֹ֣שֶׁר נְכָסִ֤ים וְכָבוֹד֙ וְאֵת֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ שֹׂנְאֶ֔יךָ וְגַם־יָמִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים לֹ֣א שָׁאָ֑לְתָּ וַתִּֽשְׁאַל־לְךָ֙ חָכְמָ֣ה וּמַדָּ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּשְׁפּוֹט֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִמְלַכְתִּ֖יךָ עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said God to Solomon, Because that was this with your heart, and not you asked wealth, riches and honor, and [the] life of those hating you, and also days many not you asked, and you asked for yourself wisdom and knowledge that you may judge my people over which I have made you king,
pieces: God said to Solomon, "Because this was what your heart desired, and you have not asked for wealth, riches or honor, or the death of those who hate you, or even for a long life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge so that you can judge {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people over whom I have made you king,

L.11: And God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for wealth, riches and honor, or the life of those who hate you, and also have not asked for many days, but have asked for yourself wisdom and knowledge so that you may judge {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people over whom I have made you king,

R.11: So God said to Solomon, "This is what you truly wanted. You did not ask to be rich or wealthy or honored. You did not ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to kill those who hate you. You did not even ask to live a long time. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge so that you can judge {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the people I have made you king over.

decisions.choice: this was in your heart: this was what you truly wanted
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and will. To say that something was "with your heart" means that it was what Solomon really wished for and intended (compare 1 Chronicles 22:7; 28:2).

decisions.choice: God's answer, worded differently from 1 Kings 3:11
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 3:11 lists what Solomon did not ask in another order: long life, wealth, the life of his enemies. Chronicles puts wealth first, adds "riches" and "honor", says "those who hate you" for "your enemies", and puts long life last. Instead of "discernment to hear justice" it repeats "wisdom and knowledge", and it adds that Yahweh made Solomon king over his people.

decisions.choice: the life of those who hate you: their death
decisions.reason: To ask for someone's life is to ask that he be put to death (as in 1 Kings 3:11). The things Solomon did not ask for are the usual wishes of kings: riches, honor, victory over their foes and long life.

decisions.choice: wealth, riches: two words for possessions
decisions.reason: The first word is the usual word for wealth; the second, found also in Joshua 22:8 and Ecclesiastes 5:18; 6:2, means possessions or goods. Together they say "great riches".

decisions.choice: Because ... , (the sentence continues in verse 12)
decisions.reason: God's sentence runs into the next verse, where its main clause comes. Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma; Readable makes short sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to kill those who hate you
decisions.reason: Readable says what asking for the life of enemies means (m3).

records.source: הַֽחָכְמָ֥ה וְהַמַּדָּ֖ע נָת֣וּן לָ֑ךְ וְעֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֤ים וְכָבוֹד֙ אֶתֶּן־לָ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀לֹא־הָ֣יָה כֵ֗ן לַמְּלָכִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־כֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: The wisdom and the knowledge [is] given to you; and wealth and riches and honor I will give to you, which not was so for the kings who [were] before you, and after you not will be so.
pieces: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. I will also give you wealth, riches and honor such as no king before you has had, and none after you will have."

L.12: the wisdom and the knowledge [are] given to you; and wealth and riches and honor I will give you, such as the kings who [were] before you did not have, and after you none will have the like."

R.12: So I am giving you wisdom and knowledge. I will also give you riches, wealth and honor. No king before you ever had so much, and no king after you will have as much."

decisions.choice: given to you: already granted
decisions.reason: The word is a passive form, "given", that describes a settled fact. God grants the request as he speaks.

decisions.choice: none like you: 1 Kings 3:12-14 in other words
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 3:12-13 God gives Solomon "a wise and discerning heart", says none before or after will be like him, and then adds wealth and honor. Chronicles says "wisdom and knowledge", and applies the comparison with kings before and after to the wealth and honor. It leaves out the promise of long life on condition of obedience (1 Kings 3:14).

decisions.choice: wealth, riches and honor: given freely
decisions.reason: Because Solomon did not ask for them, God gives them too. Verses 14-17 begin to show that this came true.

decisions.choice: the wisdom ... (lower case, continuing verse 11)
decisions.reason: This verse completes the sentence that began in verse 11, so Literal and Balanced continue it without a capital letter.

decisions.choice: No king before you ever had so much, and no king after you will have as much.
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the comparison into a sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה לַבָּמָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־בְּגִבְעוֹן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And came Solomon to the high place that [was] at Gibeon, [to] Jerusalem, from before [the] tent of meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
pieces: Then Solomon left the tent of meeting at the high place in Gibeon and came back to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.

L.13: And Solomon came [from] the high place that [was] at Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the tent of meeting, and he reigned over Israel.

R.13: Then Solomon left the meeting tent at the hilltop shrine in Gibeon and went back to Jerusalem. And he ruled as king over Israel.

decisions.choice: from the high place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "to the high place", which does not fit a journey from Gibeon to Jerusalem "from before the tent of meeting". The ancient Greek and Latin translations read "from", and the sense must be that, either because a letter was miscopied or because "came" here means "came back from [going] to". The meaning is not in doubt: Solomon returned from Gibeon.

decisions.choice: the return to Jerusalem: 1 Kings 3:15 told briefly
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 3:15 says that Solomon woke from the dream, came to Jerusalem, stood before the ark, made offerings and held a feast; then comes the case of the two women (3:16-28). Chronicles tells only the return and goes straight on to Solomon's wealth (verses 14-17), which shows God's promise of verse 12 coming true.

decisions.choice: and he reigned over Israel: the reign begins in earnest
decisions.reason: The clause sums up what follows: from Gibeon Solomon returns to rule, with the gift he asked for.

decisions.choice: left the tent of meeting at the high place in Gibeon and came back to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the places in the order of the journey; the Hebrew names the high place, then Jerusalem, then the tent.

records.source: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ וַֽיְהִי־ל֗וֹ אֶ֤לֶף וְאַרְבַּע־מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּשְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנִּיחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And gathered Solomon chariotry and horsemen, and was to him a thousand and four hundred chariot[s] and two [and] ten thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in [the] cities of the chariotry and with the king in Jerusalem.
pieces: Solomon built up a force of chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

L.14: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen; and he had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, and he stationed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.

R.14: Solomon built up a large force of chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He kept some of them in the cities where his chariots were based, and some with him in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Solomon's chariots: the same words as 1 Kings 10:26
decisions.reason: Verses 14-17 repeat, almost word for word, 1 Kings 10:26-29, where they come near the end of Solomon's story; 2 Chronicles 9:25-28 has a similar summary. Placed here, right after the promise of verse 12, they show at once the wealth and honor God gave.

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who rode or drove, or perhaps the horses themselves
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but it can also mean horses for chariots (as in 1 Kings 10:26; 5:6).

decisions.choice: the chariot cities: towns with stables and barracks for the chariot force
decisions.reason: Solomon built towns for his chariots and horsemen (8:6; 1 Kings 9:19).

decisions.choice: some ... and some with him
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 10:26: Readable says that the force was divided, and "with him" for "with the king".

records.heading: Solomon's horses and chariots

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־הַכֶּ֧סֶף וְאֶת־הַזָּהָ֛ב בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And made the king the silver and the gold in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores which [are] in the Shephelah, for abundance.
pieces: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore-fig trees of the Shephelah.

L.15: And the king made the silver and the gold in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores that [are] in the Shephelah, for abundance.

R.15: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones. Cedar wood became as plentiful as the fig trees that grow in the western foothills.

decisions.choice: silver and gold: Chronicles adds the gold
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 10:27 and 2 Chronicles 9:27 say only that the king made silver like stones. This verse adds "and the gold"; the rest is the same.

decisions.choice: like stones, like the sycamores: a deliberate overstatement
decisions.reason: Stones lay everywhere in the hills of Judah. The verse says, with poetic exaggeration, that silver, gold and costly cedar from Lebanon became as common as the most ordinary things in the land.

decisions.choice: the sycamores in the Shephelah: common fig trees of the low hills
decisions.reason: The sycamore fig bears small figs and gives cheap, ordinary timber (Isaiah 9:9; Amos 7:14). The Shephelah is the region of low hills between the coastal plain and the hill country of Judah.

decisions.choice: sycamore-fig trees of the Shephelah (Balanced); fig trees that grow in the western foothills (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 10:27: the English "sycamore" names a different tree, and Readable explains the Shephelah by where it lies.

records.source: וּמוֹצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕א סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מִקְוֵ֥א יִקְח֖וּ בִּמְחִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And [the] export of the horses which [were] to Solomon [was] from Egypt and from Kue; [the] traders of the king from Kue would take [them] at [a] price.
pieces: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders bought them from Kue at the going price.

L.16: And the export of the horses that [were] Solomon's [was] from Egypt and from Kue; the traders of the king would take [them] from Kue at a price.

R.16: Solomon's horses were brought in from Egypt and from Kue. The king's traders bought them in Kue and paid for them.

decisions.choice: the horse trade: the same words as 1 Kings 10:28
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1 Kings 10:28; only the spelling of Kue differs slightly.

decisions.choice: Kue: a land in the south of present-day Turkey
decisions.reason: Kue is known from other ancient records as a land later called Cilicia, famous for its horses. The Hebrew vowels make the name look like a word for "a gathering", and older translations read it as "in droves" or "linen yarn" (see 1 Kings 10:28). The place name fits the trade route of verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: horses from Egypt: what the law warned a king against
decisions.reason: The law of the king told him not to gather many horses or send the people back to Egypt to get them (Deuteronomy 17:16), nor to gather much silver and gold (17:17). Here, as in Kings, the horses and gold are listed without comment.

decisions.choice: imported (Balanced); brought in (Readable); bought ... at the going price
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 10:28: the Hebrew "export" looks at the horses leaving their land; Balanced and Readable look at them arriving in Israel.

records.source: וַֽ֠יַּעֲלוּ וַיּוֹצִ֨יאוּ מִמִּצְרַ֤יִם מֶרְכָּבָה֙ בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְס֖וּס בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמֵאָ֑ה וְ֠כֵן לְכָל־מַלְכֵ֧י הַֽחִתִּ֛ים וּמַלְכֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם בְּיָדָ֥ם יוֹצִֽיאוּ׃
records.gloss: And they brought up and brought out from Egypt [a] chariot for six hundred silver, and [a] horse for fifty and hundred; and thus for all [the] kings of the Hittites and [the] kings of Aram, by their hand they would bring [them] out.
pieces: They would import a chariot from Egypt for {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of silver, and a horse for {{units:about 3 3/4 pounds|150 shekels}}. In the same way they exported them, through the king's traders, to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

L.17: And they brought up and brought out from Egypt a chariot for 600 [shekels of] silver, and a horse for 150; and so for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram, by their hand they would bring [them] out.

R.17: A chariot from Egypt cost {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of silver, and a horse cost {{units:about 3 3/4 pounds|150 shekels}}. The king's traders also sold horses and chariots to all the kings of the Hittites and of Aram.

decisions.choice: the prices of chariots and horses: 1 Kings 10:29
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 10:29 says "a chariot came up and went out from Egypt"; Chronicles says "they brought up and brought out", with the traders as subject. The prices and the trade with the north are the same.

decisions.choice: 600 of silver, 150: prices in shekels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the numbers without the unit; the shekel is understood. A chariot cost four times as much as a horse.

decisions.choice: by their hand they exported: the king's traders sold them on
decisions.reason: "Their hand" refers to the king's traders of verse 16. Solomon's merchants acted as middlemen, selling horses and chariots to the kingdoms to the north.

decisions.choice: the kings of the Hittites and of Aram: the kingdoms of Syria
decisions.reason: The Hittites here are the small kingdoms of northern Syria that kept the Hittite name after the old Hittite empire fell. Aram is the land of the Arameans, north and east of Israel.

decisions.choice: 600 [shekels of] silver (Literal); about 15 pounds and about 3 3/4 pounds (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "shekels" in brackets. Balanced and Readable give the weights in modern measure, with the shekels as the alternative.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Solomon to build [a] house for [the] name of Yahweh and [a] house for his kingdom.
pieces: Solomon decided to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and a palace for his own reign.

L.18: And Solomon said [he would] build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and a house for his kingdom.

R.18: Solomon decided to build a temple where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would be worshiped, and a palace for himself as king.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in many Bibles this verse begins chapter 2
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 1 ends with this verse, and chapter 2 begins with Solomon counting out his workers. Many Bibles number this verse 2:1, and so number Hebrew 2:1-17 as 2:2-18. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: said: decided, gave orders
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word for "say". Followed by "to build" it means that Solomon declared his intention and gave the word for it (compare 1 Chronicles 21:17; 1 Kings 5:19).

decisions.choice: a house for the name of Yahweh: the temple
decisions.reason: Yahweh had said that David's son would build a house for his name (1 Chronicles 17:12; 22:10). The name stands for Yahweh himself, present among his people and called on there (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11).

decisions.choice: a house for his kingdom: a royal palace
decisions.reason: "A house for his kingdom" means a palace for his reign as king. Its building is mentioned with the temple's in 7:11 and 8:1, and described in 1 Kings 7:1-12.

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced), temple (Readable); house for his kingdom (Literal), palace for his own reign (Balanced), palace for himself as king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word "house" is used for Yahweh's temple and for the king's palace. Balanced keeps "house" for Yahweh's and says "palace" for the king's; Readable says "temple" and explains "for the name of the LORD" (m3), as 1 Kings 3:2 does.

decisions.choice: said [he would] build
decisions.reason: Literal supplies words in brackets so that "said to build" reads as English.
